headline: Editorial Mayo fue el mes de la franja y el GLP
content: Inflation theory suggests part of production cost reduction should translate to consumer prices. However, considering external factors, authorities often simplify their messages regarding measures aimed at reducing costs within financial systems. Sometimes these simplifications lead to risky outcomes such as reduced tariffs on imports including corn, milk, soybeans, etc., following revisions made last month. According to data published yesterday by INEI, sugar rose 49% nationally average – cheese and chicken breast increased too but less significantly. Perhaps June effects were seen or perhaps predictions by producers who quickly noted there wouldnt be any reductions hold true. Only time until MEF comments remains since if implemented to stimulate economy, reasons behind lack thereof need explanation. Besides failed modifications of pricing bands, high inflation in May was primarily caused by LP gas shortages leading to vehicle fuel increases up to 214%. With normalization expected soon, some decrease anticipated this month. Indeed, May had unexpectedly high inflation beyond analysts’ expectations posing risks to monetary policy set forth by BCR, suggesting belief in anchored inflationary expectations may wane.

headline: Director Editorial Javier Wa...
content: An avalanche of corruption invades us. Last week, fourteen football world figures faced bribery charges totaling over USD 150 million. This amount seems insignificant compared to billions distributed through Brazils oil giant Petrobras network involving congressional spokespeople among others. Corruption has been endemic in Latin America since colonial times. Mid-eighteenth century Captain Antonio Ulloa couldn’t curb frauds in mercury mines of Huancavelica. During Republic eras, leaders like Porfirio Diaz engaged in notorious corrupt practices ending tragically. Today, Transparency Internationals index shows highest perceived corruption levels in Somalia and North Korea while lowest in New Zealand and Namibia. Within the region, most corrupted appear Venezuela and Haiti whereas least seem Chile and Uruguay. Peru occupies intermediate position yet shouldnt cause comfort amidst spreading narcotics trade, insecurity, illegal economies, mafia influence, and institutionalized corruption pushing towards narco-state evolution. Recent cases like Orepeza, school thefts, Martin Belaunde Lossio, The Switchboard merely scratch surface showing institution weaknesses. Recent study highlights around twenty thousand regional level corruption instances recorded during 2014 marking 11% rise from previous years distinguishing three types: grand scale akin to Carlos Ilaverén cash style, medium-scale implicating directors/jobs purchasing goods/services, small-scale engaging lower ranks providing citizen services. Authors recommend aligning prevention, combatting strategies along accountability based on type targeted. For instance preventing large-scale requires international regulatory framework reinforcement whilst combating necessitates specialized investigation bodies strengthening though costly ineffective against minor where administrative regulation alongside participation transparency mechanisms suffice.

headline: Análisis Fiscal
